rv.q: LIFE AFTER is a stunning and original new musical that left me fully emotional.
'Life After,' on the other hand, will stay with you for a long while.
This show, with this cast and orchestra, is as perfect as musicals get.
It's a lovely, funny, painful, and beautiful musical—its final numbers, 'Snow' and 'Poetry,' absolutely stun, as does Williams' performance as she sings them.
Life After is a satisfying choice for those who have lost or may lose someone precious without perfecting their last moments together.
Overall, this musical is worth going to see. There was not a moment where I found myself looking away from the stage; I was always excited to see what would happen next.
Unfortunately, the combination of characters using satire and sorrow throughout this play is somewhat enigmatic and perplexing and causes a loss in translation to what is a very stunning narrative.
Despite those wrinkles, Johnson's LIFE AFTER was an interesting and unique twist on dealing with a fatality. I enjoyed it!

It is unrelentingly loud to the point where a numbing effect sets in. And while the show’s seven-piece orchestra, led by music director and keyboardist Chris Kong, also has a powerful “voice” (with orchestrations by Lynne Shankel) it, too, is relentlessly loud.
Every aspect of the production – the cast, the music and lyrics, set and stage design and costumes, is wonderful.
"Life After" is a strong story that is emotionally moving for most people. I suggest bringing at least three tissues with you for this one.
